//: ApexPricing AI Retail Pricing Engine — HTTP API inventory.
//purpose: Two groups: (A) endpoints that EXIST and are verified working, and (B) endpoints that DO NOT EXIST YET but are genuinely needed. Every entry has a 'why' field explaining what it is for. Group B also carries 'needed' to say whether its absence is currently breaking anything.
//comments: JSON has no native comment syntax, so explanations live in '_why' / '_notes' keys. All '_'-prefixed keys are documentation, not data.
//on_missing_apis: IMPORTANT HONESTY NOTE: after the backend fixes in this session, the app has NO API whose absence breaks a working feature. Every gap below is an enhancement, not a blocker. They are listed because the product claims capabilities (in README/changes.md) that no endpoint serves.

meta.//base_url: api/main.py mounts frontend/ at '/', so a page opened from that server has no CORS problem. api_base in the frontend is the literal '/api'.
meta.//spec_url: FastAPI auto-generates OpenAPI docs. This is the authoritative live schema and needs no extra work.
meta.//model_sources: Both the ?model_source= query parameter on the GET endpoints and the model_source request-body field are typed as a Literal. Any value outside this list is rejected with HTTP 422 instead of silently falling back to 'synthetic'.
meta.//model_sources_history: Only the POST body was validated in the first fix round; the GET query parameter was still a plain string and returned 200 for unknown values, which contradicted an earlier version of this file. Both are now validated. This is noted so a reader does not have to trust the claim blindly.

existing_endpoints.returns: Portfolio KPIs: total_skus, total_inventory_units, total_inventory_value, total_status_quo_profit, total_optimized_profit, total_profit_lift, avg_profit_lift_pct, action_counts, risk_counts, model_source, as_of, training_metadata
existing_endpoints.consumed_by: frontend/js/app.js -> loadData() (the four KPI ribbon slots + provenance badge)

existing_endpoints._why: Single request that powers the Executive Overview headline numbers so the page does not compute aggregates client-side.

existing_endpoints.returns: {status, data[], active_events[], model_source}. Each data row: product_id, current_price, recommended_price, price_action, current_inventory, days_to_successor, mrp, unit_cost, expected_lifecycle_profit, profit_lift_amount, inventory_risk_level, memo, xai, elasticity, feasible_prices[], profit_curve[], demand_curve[] (+_lower/_upper conformal bands), current_price_source, inventory_source
existing_endpoints.consumed_by: the SKU Matrix table, the Competitor Radar table, the transfers view, the simulator and the XAI modal

existing_endpoints._why: The core payload of the whole product: one constrained-optimisation result per SKU, self-describing enough that the UI needs no other call for the catalogue.
The 'Sync Data' / 'Re-Calculate All' / 'Recalculate Engine' buttons need a way to force recomputation. Now also re-reads the CSVs and invalidates BOTH model-source caches.

existing_endpoints.note: Alias of the GET for clients that prefer POST for mutations. Both are registered.
existing_endpoints._why: Kept because the frontend issues it as POST.
Lets the UI show the market-signal banner and badge SKUs whose lifecycle horizon was shortened by a real announcement.

existing_endpoints._body_notes: days_to_successor must be > 0 and <= 3650 (422 otherwise). competitor_price_drop_pct must be within 0..1.
existing_endpoints.verified: HTTP 200. Horizon shifts 60 -> 14 and the SKU flips to a Clearance Markdown at a lowered price.
existing_endpoints._why: Simulates ingesting a breaking keynote announcement so the lifecycle horizon can be shortened and the pricing response observed live. Applied as an in-memory override; no CSV is ever rewritten.

existing_endpoints.verified: HTTP 200 and the SKU horizon returns to its 60-day baseline.
existing_endpoints._why: Reverts every lifecycle override so the demo can be re-run from a clean state.

existing_endpoints.returns: {status, method, snapshot_date, data[]} — per-SKU LP transportation plan with stores_summary and recommended_transfers
existing_endpoints._why: Exposes the multi-store transfer optimiser, which is otherwise invisible: it decides whether moving stock between branches earns more than it costs in logistics.

existing_endpoints._body_notes: price must be > 0. inventory must be >= 0 (0 is valid and now honoured). All optional context fields fall back to the SKU's real values from the CSVs when omitted.
existing_endpoints.returns: {status, product_id, model_source, simulated_price, requested_price, price_clamped_to_mrp, mrp, unit_cost, daily_demand, daily_demand_lower, daily_demand_upper, expected_sales, leftover_inventory, projected_revenue, holding_and_finance_cost, depreciation_loss, expected_net_profit, expected_net_profit_lower, expected_net_profit_upper, clearance_days, clearance_probability, margin_per_unit}
existing_endpoints.consumed_by: frontend/js/app.js -> fetchBackendSimulation(), debounced 180 ms behind the price slider
existing_endpoints.verified: HTTP 200 with full context. Values now agree with the chart (both compute the same net profit at the same price, within the residual difference between the endpoint's and the optimiser's cost models).
existing_endpoints._why: Answers 'what happens if I charge this price?' with the exact money breakdown (revenue, carrying cost, depreciation, net) instead of the client's own approximation. Sending the SKU's real inventory/horizon/competitor prices is essential, otherwise the endpoint's defaults make the tiles contradict the plotted curve.
api/main.py mounts the static frontend at the root so the UI and API share one origin and CORS never applies in normal use.

missing_endpoints._why: Would let the UI show real engine provenance instead of the hardcoded sidebar telemetry ('CORE ENGINE LGBM-2.4-M', 'LATENCY < 2.1ms'). Those two values are currently unmeasured literals. Should return: status, model_source(s) loaded, model file mtime, artefact availability, dataset 'as_of' date, and measured p50 request latency.
missing_endpoints._impact_today: Cosmetic but it is a credibility problem in a technical seminar: the UI displays latency and version figures that nothing verifies.

missing_endpoints._why: The README advertises a competitor-intelligence module, and data/synthetic/competitors.csv holds per-date, per-channel prices (Amazon/Flipkart/Croma/Vijay Sales) plus availability. Today only a single latest-date aggregate is folded into /api/optimizations, so no price-history or per-channel view is possible. Needed for: a real Competitor Radar, gap-over-time charts, and a stockout opportunity detector.
missing_endpoints._impact_today: The Competitor Radar table works (it reads the aggregate off /api/optimizations), but it can only ever show one snapshot and one averaged price per SKU.

missing_endpoints._why: The README advertises an inventory-risk module, but there is no endpoint for it. A proper version should return per-SKU, per-store exposure: days-to-successor countdown, stranded units, capital tied up, depreciation write-down at risk, and days-of-supply by branch. It must be store-granular, which /api/optimizations is not.
missing_endpoints._impact_today: Risk is only a single label per SKU ('Low Risk' / 'Stockout'). The stranded-capital maths that the lifecycle model already computes internally is not surfaced as its own view, so the depreciation argument — the core of the product pitch — is invisible.

missing_endpoints._why: There is no way to fetch one SKU's full detail or its history. Needed for deep-linking to a SKU, a detail drawer, and audit trails. The /api/optimizations payload already carries almost everything per SKU, so this is a convenience/robustness endpoint rather than new computation.
missing_endpoints._impact_today: None — the UI holds the whole catalogue in memory. It becomes necessary if the catalogue grows past a few hundred SKUs and shipping the full array to the browser stops being sensible.

missing_endpoints._why: src/optimization/price_path_generator.py builds a phased multi-week markdown schedule, but no endpoint exposes it. The README claims a phased pricing roadmap. Without this, that module is dead code from the product's point of view.
missing_endpoints._impact_today: A genuine capability the team already built is unreachable from the UI.

missing_endpoints._why: No export affordance exists anywhere. A retailer (or a seminar examiner) cannot take the recommendation set away. docs/Retailer_User_Guide.pdf and the CSV import templates already exist, so the export is the missing half of that workflow.
missing_endpoints._impact_today: Users must read numbers off the screen or scrape the JSON by hand.

missing_endpoints._why: Per-SKU elasticity is computed (model-derived via finite differences, with an OLS diagnostic) and embedded in each /api/optimizations row, but there is no endpoint to inspect the estimate's quality: raw beta, p-value, R-squared and whether the estimate was identifiable at all. That diagnostics detail is exactly what a technical audience asks about.
missing_endpoints._impact_today: The `elasticity_method` string is shown, but the statistical evidence behind it is not retrievable.

fixes_that_removed_api_needs: POST /api/simulate was being called at '/undefined/simulate' because the frontend referenced this.apiBase instead of API_BASE. Fixed in frontend; no API change was needed.
The same call sent model_source from this.state.dataSource (undefined) so it always claimed 'synthetic'. Now sends the real source.
The simulator now sends inventory, days_to_successor, competitor_avg_price and competitor_min_price, so the endpoint no longer falls back to its own defaults and the tiles agree with the chart.
A sold-out SKU (0 units on hand) is now returned as price_action='No Stock' with risk 'Stockout' instead of a phantom 'Clearance Markdown' at an invented price.
risk_counts now sums to the SKU count and uses one vocabulary that matches the rows it summarises.
avg_profit_lift_pct is null rather than a sign-inverted ratio when the status-quo baseline is non-positive.
Both model-source caches are invalidated together, so a lifecycle event can no longer leave a stale summary on the other source.
Request validation now rejects negative or zero price, negative inventory/horizon, and unknown model_source with HTTP 422 instead of returning 200 with impossible numbers.
